# brig service create

Create and start a service

## Synopsis

```text
brig service create NAME --type TYPE
```

## Description

Create a service of a type that [`brig service types`](brig-service-types.md) lists, and start it. A
service of placement vm gets a VM called NAME, made like [`brig create`](brig-create.md) makes
one; its CPUs, memory and network profile come from the flags, else from the
type, else from config.yaml. Its OpenShell config directories are only the
ones that --openshell-config names, never openshell.configs from config.yaml,
so that the service VM holds no secrets but its own. They bind the
service's secrets in services/NAME.yaml.

brig picks a port on the host's loopback interface for the service, which
stays the same for its life: gateways reach the service there, and
sandboxes at http://host.openshell.internal:PORT.

--binary replaces the type's programs that may call the service from a
sandbox; OpenShell adds a sandbox's token only to their requests.

## Examples

```sh
brig service create mirror --type http-mirror --openshell-config ~/brig/mirror
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--binary stringArray` | absolute path of a program that may call the service from a sandbox (repeatable; default: the type's) |
| `--cpus int` | number of virtual CPUs of the service VM |
| `--memory size` | memory size of the service VM, e.g. 4GiB |
| `--no-start` | create the service without starting it |
| `--openshell-config stringArray` | OpenShell config directory of the service VM (repeatable) |
| `-o, --output format` | output format: table or json (default `table`) |
| `--profile string` | network profile of the service VM (see config.yaml) |
| `--type string` | the service's type (see brig service types) |
| `--wait` | fail unless the gateway answers and the OpenShell config directories sync |

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.
